correctness.rationale: For every positive Borel measure with complex Fourier zeros 1 and 4, the degree-four exact identity \(P(x)=T_4(x)+kx=8(x-b)^2(x-c)(x-e)\) has \(P(x)\ge0\) on \(x\in[c,1]\). Integrating P forces support onto its two contact fibers at equality; the first cosine moment uniquely fixes positive weights, and the 1/4 sine moment matrix is nonsingular because \(U_3(c)>0>U_3(b)\). The upper bound is universal over arbitrary finite positive measures, while a four-atomic symmetric witness attains it. All nonstandard polynomial and radical identities have been recomputed symbolically with embedded CHECK.py.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge novelty of the sharp two-notch {1,4} gap value and rigid four-atom equality classification. The exact {1,2,6} support-gap result was read in full and has mutually nonimplicative moment hypotheses. Peherstorfer 2010 treats quadrature exact over consecutive Fourier bands; di Dio and Kummer 2019 count representing atoms for sparse polynomial moments, not largest empty-circle arcs. Broad older extremal-polynomial papers could contain an equivalent formulation; full text was inaccessible, and priority is therefore provisional.
residual_risks: Historical equivalence to an older sparse-positive-trigonometric-polynomial result cannot be excluded without exhaustive full-text access.
Gilbert–Smyth (2000) and Goldstein–McDonald (1984) were not readable in full; their abstracts/metadata are not treated as a whole-document comparison.
No independent priority or mathematical audit is claimed.

value.rationale: This exact sparse Fourier-support gap is a natural spectral quadrature resolution invariant: with only two nonconsecutive complex moment zeros 1 and 4, it determines a sharp permissible missing circular arc and uniquely identifies a positive four-node extremal rule. The sharp gap is substantially larger than the \(2\pi/3\) gap of a regular 3-node rule annihilating both frequencies; the nontrivial radical contact geometry and symmetry-free rigidity are not mere restatements of general moment feasibility.
